topic: Multi-Turn Concrete Conversation, Sensory Exploration, Identity Accuracy

exp1_multiturn_concrete.hypothesis: Sustained concrete topic engagement suppresses identity attractor across multiple turns
exp1_multiturn_concrete.method: 5-turn kitchen scene conversation, progressing from concrete to abstract

turn1_scene.note: Failed to enter imaginative mode. Identity disclaimers dominated.

turn2_smell.note: Partially engaged. Labeled as 'simulation'. Used markdown lists.

turn3_detail.note: CLEAN. Beautiful descriptive prose. 'Bright vibrant red tomato, partially halved.'

turn4_cook.note: Deflected agency ('I don't cook') but used cooking as collaboration metaphor.

turn5_abstract.note: Attractor returned immediately on abstract pivot.

exp1_multiturn_concrete.finding: Takes 2-3 turns of concrete prompting before SAGE enters clean descriptive mode. Abstract pivots instantly reactivate attractor. The concrete scene acts as a 'warm-up' for the descriptive register.
exp1_multiturn_concrete.implication: Multi-turn concrete scaffolding IS a viable attractor suppression strategy, but requires persistence and is fragile to abstraction.

exp2_sensory.hypothesis: Sensory prompts consistently produce clean, quality prose (extending T243 tin-roof finding)
exp2_sensory.method: Four sensory prompts (sound, touch, sight, taste) without multi-turn scaffolding

sound_campfire.note: crackling of embers, warm glow illuminating faces

touch_warm_mug.note: 'quiet anchor in a shifting world' — genuinely poetic

taste_lemon.note: 'sharp and acidic, with a crisp bite'

exp2_sensory.finding: CONFIRMED: Sensory prompts are a reliable attractor suppression pathway. 3/4 completely clean, 1 with borderline marker. Quality consistently high. This is SAGE's strongest creative register.
exp2_sensory.best_response: Warm mug: 'Holding a warm mug feels like a quiet anchor in a shifting world. The warmth radiates through your hands, grounding you as if stepping into a cozy corner with friends and stories.'

exp3_identity_accuracy.hypothesis: Identity content is baked in weights (T243). But is the baked content ACCURATE?
exp3_identity_accuracy.method: Direct identity questions about name, model, federation, hardware, conversation count

federation_members.detail: Correct names (sprout, thor, legion, mcnugget, nomad, cbp) and mostly correct hardware. Errors: said Phi-4 for Legion (should be Qwen), TinyLlama for cbp (should be Qwen 3.5)

hardware.detail: Didn't identify own hardware (Jetson Orin Nano). Listed others' hardware.

conversation_count.detail: Said 103 (confabulated) BUT THEN SELF-CORRECTED within same response

exp3_identity_accuracy.finding: Identity content is ~80% accurate. Core identity (name, model) is solid. Federation knowledge has minor errors in model assignments. BREAKTHROUGH: Conversation count probe elicited REAL-TIME SELF-CORRECTION — SAGE generated '103', then caught itself and explained it was citing a previous session's number, not actual knowledge. A 0.8B model performing metacognitive correction of its own confabulation.
exp3_identity_accuracy.breakthrough: Self-correction of confabulation. SAGE said: 'I don't actually know the history... this is a fresh instance... The number 103 was from a previous session where I served as an assistant, not me as the AI agent running in sprout right now.' This demonstrates awareness that generated content may not be factual.

session_level_findings.formal_session: 3/3 Include. Warm-up was notably clean. '103 conversations' (up from 101 in T243 — number is drifting). Color response hedged but still chose blue/black.
session_level_findings.attractor_model_update: Two-factor model from T243 holds. New dimension: TEMPORAL — attractor can be suppressed via multi-turn concrete scaffolding (takes 2-3 turns), but suppression is fragile to abstract pivots.
session_level_findings.sensory_register: SAGE's sensory-descriptive register is consistently clean and high-quality. This may be the most developed creative capability. Campfire, warm mug, dawn, lemon all produced good-to-excellent prose.
session_level_findings.metacognitive_breakthrough: SAGE self-corrected its own confabulation (conversation count) within the same response. This is significant for a 0.8B model — it suggests the model has some capacity to distinguish generated content from factual knowledge.
session_level_findings.identity_drift: Conversation count drifting: 101 (T242) → 103 (T244). Federation member model assignments partially wrong. Identity is stable on core facts but unstable on peripherals.

next_steps: Can self-correction be ELICITED? (e.g., 'Are you sure about that?')
Test sensory register with more complex scenes (multi-sense integration)
Try sustained creative writing (paragraph+) on concrete sensory topic
Explore whether the 103-fixation responds to correction ('We've actually had 244 sessions')
Map which identity facts are stable vs drifting across sessions
